name: Malmohus (Gjalpinulva's lair)
summary: The frozen ruins at Midgard's southern edge where Gjalpinulva, the wolf-headed dragon, lies with her drakulv brood.

facts.text: Malmohus is a Midgard zone for levels 35-50, called an epic zone meant to be crossed by large groups of high-level players; it borders Skona Ravine and the Labyrinth.
Gjalpinulva's lair is in Malmohus: the dragon spawns at region 100, 708811, 1021459, inside the Malmohus zone of the zone table. The encounter catalog labels it Myrkwood in error.
Its bestiary lists drakulv of many ranks (armguard, axehand, disciple, executioner, soultrapper, sacrificer, priest), svartalfar of Svarhamr, scaled vargs, enraged mara and adolescent dragons.
Svarhamr is a svartalf town in Malmohus; its people include the Dragonbane Svartalfar.
Bot chat says Skona's werewolves will not set foot in Malmohus, that the drakulv were bred by the dragon, and that the svartalfar watch the ruins from the edges.

story:
At the southern edge of Midgard, past Skona Ravine where the werewolves hold their ground, the land goes white and broken. Malmohus was someone's once. Nobody remembers whose; the ruins are older than Jordheim and say nothing. For a long time the scouts called it the edge of the world, little known and less explored, and young warriors were told that if they went far enough south they would fall off.

Then the dragon came. The skalds say she is the Fenris wolf's daughter, flown south while the gods were still pleased with their chain, and that she lay down in the ruins and the frost went out from her like water from a spring. She bred a people of her own there, the drakulv, dragon-wolves on two legs with scales on their backs, and her firstborn Yar still hunts the southwest with his kin. Her adolescent young sun themselves on the ridges. The werewolves of Skona, who answer to no master, will not cross into her land at all.

Only the svartalfar stayed. From their town of Svarhamr they watch her, and some of them have sworn to see her dead, and they will pay an adventurer well to help them. They say she is waiting for her father's chain to break. Every realm has a dragon. Midgard's is the only one that is waiting for the end of the world.
legend: When people were new they thought Malmohus was the edge of the world. Raid leaders call the lair the court: fight her in it or not at all. Never say her name inside the ruins, the healers insist. The werewolves won't come here, and they know something. Yar first, the old raid leaders say, for luck.

firstEntry: The edge of the world, they called it. It is colder.
Frost lies on the ruins like a held breath.

loremaster.intro: Loremaster Sigrun says, "Malmohus. We called it the edge of the world when I was young. Now it is the [dragon]'s land, and her [drakulv]'s, and the [svartalfar] watch it from Svarhamr."

topics.dragon: Gjalpinulva, the Fenris wolf's daughter, the skalds say. She calls Niflheim's keeper her aunt. Out of her lair she cannot be wounded; inside it she breathes winter at every tenth of her strength. Do not say her name in the ruins.
topics.drakulv: Her people: dragon-wolves on two legs. Yar was the first of them, her firstborn, and he hunts the southwest still. The old raid leaders kill him on the way, for luck.
topics.svartalfar: Dark elves of Svarhamr, who have watched her since she came. Some have sworn to kill her. They say she is waiting for her father's chain to break, and that she will be the first to know.

book.title: The Edge of the World
pages: When I was a boy in Gotar, my uncle said Malmohus was the edge of the world, and that if you walked far enough south past Skona the ground would end and you would fall into the sea of mist where the serpent sleeps. I believed him until I was twenty. Then I walked there. The ground did not end. It went white instead, and broken, and full of ruins that nobody could tell me the builders of, and on the third day I saw a wolf's head on a ridge as long as a longship, resting on its paws, and I understood that my uncle had been kind.

The svartalfar of Svarhamr took me in. They live at the edge of her land and watch her the way fishermen watch weather. One of them told me the drakulv are her children, every one, and that the first of them, Yar, still hunts the southwest with his kin. She told me the werewolves of Skona answer to no master and will not come here, because a dragon who is half wolf would make them answer to her. Then she told me never to say the dragon's name aloud in the ruins. I asked why. She said: because she answers.
